notes: The 3 separate groups are real and are kept on purpose. Set 40181 is three models: the pizza shop (steps 1-24), the white delivery van (steps 25-31) and the brown truck (steps 32-37). The booklet never joins them (page 22 shows them standing beside each other), so adding a connection would be wrong.

The booklet is isometric, so every x/y/layer value is my estimate. The shop is on a grid 6 wide (x) by 8 deep (y). The front is y=0 and the awning faces front. x=0 is the front-left. The 6x8 base plate p64 is turned=true so it covers x0..5, y0..7.
The van and truck are placed beside the shop (x>=7) at layer 0 only to keep them on a grid. They do not touch the shop.
Booklet steps are numbered continuously: shop 1-24, van 25-31, truck 32-37.

The booklet's part pictures were matched to piece-list ids by colour and shape. Examples: the three clear 1x2 plates in the van, the 1x2 clear window plates, and the black round 1x1 plates used as wheels.

Wheels (black round plates) and the two Technic pins are not on the stud grid, so position is null. They are listed in other_joins. Each wheel is attached to a clip plate; the exact wheel-to-clip pairing is assumed.
The red studded brick p1 is drawn without anything clearly under it, so rests_on is empty. The roof p86 sits on it, which keeps it attached. The pizza tile p103 attaches to it through other_joins.
The tooth plate p105, the window-stack plate p51, and the exact layout of the upper brown courses, red plates and white curved bricks are best estimates from small isometric drawings.
The 1x1 stacks (clear, clear, red) are recorded as stacked plates. The 1x2 stack (clear, clear, red 1x2) in steps 7 and 18 is recorded the same way.
